channel.title: Hack Tracker
channel.description: Confirmed hacking incidents and outages people suspected were hacks, with official explanations and sources.

item.title: StubHub International (ticket resale) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: StubHub International, the non-U.S. ticket resale business run by Ticketbis, told customers it detected unauthorized access to certain systems between late October and early November. Impact: Customer names, email addresses, phone numbers and country or region settings may have been exposed. The company says it found no evidence passwords, banking information or payment card details were accessed. It has not said how many customers were affected. Status: Confirmed by StubHub International. Investigation ongoing with outside experts. Sources: The Register (https://www.theregister.com/cyber-crime/2026/11/18/stubhub-international-warns-customer-data-may-have-left-the-venue/5310775)

item.title: Ethiopian Airlines — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Ethiopian Airlines emailed members of its ShebaMiles frequent-flyer program warning that some customer information may have been exposed in a recent cyberattack it called "of limited scope." Impact: The airline says there is currently no evidence financial information was accessed. It has not said when the intrusion happened, what data was involved or how many people are affected. Status: Confirmed by Ethiopian Airlines. Investigation ongoing with authorities. Sources: TechCabal (https://techcabal.com/2026/11/18/ethiopian-airlines-reports-cyberattack/)

item.title: Equinor (energy company, Norway) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Norway's state-controlled oil and gas giant said it detected an ongoing cyberattack against some of its IT systems and was working to neutralise it. Impact: Some IT systems affected; staff may have trouble reaching corporate apps and IT services. Equinor says there are no indications data was stolen, the attack did not involve a computer virus, and oil and gas production was not affected. Status: Confirmed by Equinor. Work to neutralise the attack and restore systems ongoing; Equinor says it is too early to say how long that will take. Sources: Equinor statement (https://www.equinor.com/news/20261711-equinor-detected-cyber-attack); Reuters via Euronext (https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/norways-equinor-detects-ongoing-cyberattack-oil-and-gas-output-unaffected); The Record (https://therecord.media/norway-equinor-cyberattack-energy)

item.title: Visa (via third-party provider) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A new ransomware gang called n0n listed Visa on its leak site and set a 48-hour deadline to publish data it claims to have stolen. Visa confirmed an incident, but says it started at an unnamed third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region. Impact: Visa says its own systems were not involved or impacted and there is no indication payment data such as card numbers was affected. What the gang claims to have taken has not been shown. Status: Third-party incident confirmed by Visa. Gang's data claims unverified. Sources: Cybernews (https://cybernews.com/security/visa-jpmorgan-data-breach/); CISO Brief (https://cisobrief.com/visa-confirms-third-party-incident-as-n0n-ransomware-gang-also-lists-jpmorgan-chase/)

item.title: SOFT99 (car care products, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Unauthorized access to an outside company that handles SOFT99's online-shop orders and shipping leaked customer order information. Impact: About 3,813 people (3,728 orders): names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and order details. No card data. All online shops temporarily closed. Status: Confirmed by SOFT99. Police and regulator notified. Sources: Japan IR (SOFT99 disclosure) (https://japanir.jp/en/company/company-4464/ir/4464-20261117-01_wp_disclosure_update/)

item.title: Wilmington School District 209U (Illinois) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The district's superintendent told families the district was hit by a ransomware attack that may have involved a data breach. Impact: District laptops and other Windows devices suspended as a precaution; internet, Chromebooks and phones still usable. Whether personal information was accessed is still being determined. Status: Confirmed by the district. Investigation ongoing with cybersecurity specialists. Sources: WJOL (https://www.wjol.com/wilmington-school-district-209u-reports-ransomware-attack-and-possible-data-breach/)

item.title: Apple services outage (iCloud, App Store, Apple Pay) — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: iCloud sign-in, the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare and Apple retail store systems went down for hours, the latest in a week of big U.S. outages. What people speculated: Another hit in a coordinated cyberattack behind the Microsoft, FAA, Chase and NSA outages. Official explanation: Apple said an internal update caused the outages and that it was not a cyberattack. The U.S. Director of National Intelligence also said the recent string of outages was not a cyberattack or a coordinated nation-state effort. Impact: Hours of sign-in failures and service outages; Apple stores unable to complete purchases. Services restored by that evening. Status: Company explanation given. Not a hack. Sources: MacRumors (https://www.macrumors.com/2026/11/17/apple-outage-internal-update/); NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/business/corporations/apple-outages-working-get-systems-back-online-rcna609861); CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/apple-microsoft-faa-jpmorgan-outages.html)

item.title: NSA classified network (NSANet) — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: The National Security Agency's internal top-secret network went down, right on the heels of a week of big outages. What people speculated: An attack on a U.S. intelligence network. Official explanation: The NSA described it as scheduled maintenance; news reports say it happened during a software update to patch the system, with no evidence of a cyberattack. Impact: Temporary loss of the agency's internal classified communications network. Status: Official explanation given. No evidence of a hack. Sources: NSA statement (https://www.nsa.gov/Press-Room/Press-Releases-Statements/Press-Release-View/Article/4650245/nsa-statement-on-network-issues/); CBS News (https://www.cbsnews.com/news/nsa-network-down-classified-fort-meade/); The Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/17/nsa-national-security-classified-communications-network-down)

item.title: Marriott Bonvoy sign-in outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Marriott.com and the Bonvoy app wouldn't let members sign in for several hours, knocking out mobile check-in and digital room keys for some guests. What people speculated: Part of a wave of attacks behind the week's other outages. Official explanation: Marriott said it resolved a technical issue and its review found no indication it was cybersecurity-related. Impact: Several hours of failed log-ins, mobile keys and reservation changes. Status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack. Sources: Skift (https://skift.com/2026/11/17/marriott-bonvoy-sign-ins-were-down-for-hours-disrupting-mobile-keys/); AP News (https://apnews.com/article/apple-marriott-technology-outages-ff097d2a0bec767baf38a1bd8eff5829)

item.title: Optimizely (website experimentation platform) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into scripts that run on customers' websites. Researchers at Report URI found the code on 178 organizations' sites, including big names like Salesforce, Zoom, HSBC, CNN and Ikea, so visitors to those sites were exposed without the companies themselves being breached. Impact: Per Report URI, the malware swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and tried to deliver iOS exploit kits to iPhones and iPads; at least $7,000 in crypto was traced as stolen. Most of the malicious code was removed the same day. Status: Confirmed by Optimizely. In a Nov. 18 update it said under 5% of its customers were affected, the flaw (in its Web Experimentation sign-up flow) was closed within three hours of detection, and all injected code has been removed. Sources: The Record (https://therecord.media/optimizely-malicious-code-customer-sites); TechTarget (https://www.techtarget.com/news/optimizely-supply-chain-attack-turns-trusted-scripts-against-178-orgs/874997/); Security Today (https://securitytoday.com/articles/2026/11/18/optimizely-patches-signup-flaw-after-attackers-inject-malicious-code.aspx)

item.title: South Korea government email system — Confirmed Hack
item.description: South Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety said hackers got into the government's administrative email system by going through vulnerable local government networks and exploiting a flaw in its single sign-on (SSO) login system. Impact: Abnormal access to about 300 government email accounts found so far. The breach was reported to the privacy regulator and affected people were notified. Status: Confirmed by South Korea's government. Joint investigation with NIS and KISA ongoing. Sources: SBS News (https://news.sbs.co.kr/english/article.do?news_id=N1008847830); Aju Press (https://www.ajupress.com/view/20261116133270131)

item.title: Infoblox (network security company) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The networking and security company confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor. Impact: Infoblox says there's no indication its products, cloud services or software updates were involved. The Register reports, citing an internal email, that employee personal details (including Social Security numbers and direct-deposit details) and some customers' network configuration backups were taken; Infoblox has not said how many customers are affected. Status: Confirmed by Infoblox. Investigation ongoing. Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/16/cyber-giant-infoblox-confirms-security-incident-after-hackers-access-company-information/); TechRadar (https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/infoblox-confirms-company-and-customer-data-exposed-in-sharepoint-breach)

item.title: Charleston County Government (South Carolina) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Charleston County's IT team spotted unusual network activity and the county has confirmed data was removed from its systems. State police (SLED) are investigating on site. Impact: Data removed; the county is still determining whether personal or financial information was involved. Day-to-day operations not affected. Status: Confirmed by Charleston County. Investigation ongoing. Sources: Moultrie News / Post and Courier (https://www.postandcourier.com/moultrie-news/news/charleston-co-comments-on-cybersecurity-attack/article_38ccf8e5-2ae0-470a-a900-48eaf6315a0a.html)

item.title: JPMorgan Chase online banking — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Chase's online banking slowed and transactions were delayed for hours, with knock-on delays at other banks. It was the fourth big U.S. outage in five days, which fed questions about a coordinated attack. On Nov 17 a new ransomware gang, n0n, listed JPMorgan Chase on its leak site, claiming it stole data; that is an unverified attacker claim. What people speculated: A cyberattack on the banking system, possibly linked to the Microsoft and FAA outages. Official explanation: Chase blamed a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware and said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. Asked about the gang's claim, the bank said there is no evidence linking the disruption to a cyberattack. Impact: Delayed transactions and online banking problems; some other banks affected when dealing with Chase. Status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack. Sources: POLITICO (https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/16/jpmorgan-chase-banking-outage-software-bug-01168592); CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/jpmorgan-chase-technical-issue.html); Cybernews (https://cybernews.com/security/visa-jpmorgan-data-breach/)

item.title: United Airlines system outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Three days after the FAA ground stop, a United system outage delayed departures because pilots couldn't get final aircraft weight data needed for takeoff. What people speculated: Another attack on U.S. aviation, linked to the FAA ground stop. Official explanation: United said it was a technology issue, resolved in about an hour and a half, with no indication of a cyberattack or link to the ground stop. Impact: Delays to hundreds of departures. Status: No root cause published. No evidence of a hack. Sources: CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/united-airlines-outage-faa.html); AP News (https://apnews.com/article/united-airlines-outage-5a5e5f75bb07f11ffb8750901f0076ff); CNA (https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/united-airlines-says-tech-outage-disrupts-departures-no-signs-cyberattack-6556946)

item.title: Nikkei (via PLAID KARTE marketing service) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that Nikkei uses, was accessed without authorization, and some Nikkei Online Edition user data it handled may have leaked. Impact: Email addresses, phone numbers, gender and birth year/month, which Nikkei says had been processed so they can't be restored to their original form. No card data. Status: Confirmed by Nikkei. Sources: Nikkei announcement (https://www.nikkei.co.jp/nikkeiinfo/en/news/announcements/1576.html)

item.title: City of South Portland (Maine) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The city shut down its network after discovering a cybersecurity issue; its preliminary assessment points to cybercriminal activity. Impact: City Hall, Assessing and the Library closed to the public while systems are restored. The city says initial assessments show most city data is unaffected. Status: Confirmed by the city. Forensic review ongoing with state and federal agencies. Sources: City of South Portland (https://www.southportland.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/619)

item.title: PLAID KARTE customers (MUFG Bank, JINS, Shimamura and others, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in servers run by PLAID, the Tokyo company behind the KARTE customer-data marketing service, stole credentials used to connect to its systems and databases, and read data out. They also took over a PLAID account to get into the admin console. PLAID shut down all KARTE services on Nov. 13, and companies that use KARTE have been announcing leaks of their own customers' data since. Impact: Varies by company. MUFG Bank: about 6.5 million records of gender, age and region (no names or contact details). JINS: up to about 18.29 million accounts (email, surname, birth date and more). Shimamura: about 7 million members' birth dates, gender, prefecture and postal code. RIZAP: up to about 4.32 million email addresses. J.League: about 2.38 million ticketing records (internal user IDs, birth dates, gender, prefecture and city). Stripe International: about 150,000 STRIPE CLUB records with email addresses and member IDs. PLAID also says credentials used to link KARTE to outside services leaked, and has asked customers to revoke them. Status: Confirmed by PLAID and affected companies. KARTE still offline with no restart date as of Nov. 18. Sources: MUFG Bank notice (Japanese, PDF) (https://www.bk.mufg.jp/news/news2026/pdf/news1118.pdf); ITmedia NEWS (Japanese) (https://www.itmedia.co.jp/news/article/2611/18/2000003287/); J.League notice (Japanese) (https://www.jleague.jp/news/article/35384/)

item.title: DHC (cosmetics, Japan, via PLAID KARTE) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Unauthorized access to KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that DHC used for direct mail and similar messages, leaked DHC customer account information linked to it. PLAID notified DHC on Nov. 13. Impact: About 19.11 million customer account records (names, email addresses, birth dates and more). DHC says online-shop passwords and card data were not included and no secondary damage has been confirmed. Status: Confirmed by DHC. Regulator to be notified. Sources: Nikkei (Japanese) (https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXZQOUC1886Z0Y6A111C2000000/)

item.title: FAA: nationwide ground stop — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: The FAA halted departures across the U.S. for more than four hours after its air traffic communications network became unstable. It came one day after the big Microsoft outage, so many people asked whether the two were linked or whether someone had hacked the system. What people speculated: A hack or coordinated attack on air traffic control, possibly connected to the Microsoft outage the day before. Official explanation: The FAA says it has "no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor." Its explanation: after a contractor installed a new router at a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, data flooded the FAA's legacy network (with a second problem site in Amarillo, Texas). Officials said it was not related to the Microsoft outage. Impact: Instability at 17 of 22 en route air traffic control centers; about 12,462 flights canceled that day (FAA figure). Status: No evidence of a hack. Root-cause investigation ongoing. Sources: FAA: Nationwide Ground Stop Q&A (https://www.faa.gov/newsroom/nationwide-ground-stop-questions-and-answers); SecurityWeek (https://www.securityweek.com/no-signs-of-hacking-in-faa-ground-stop-as-fbi-reportedly-probes-software-update/); AP News (https://apnews.com/article/nationwide-ground-stop-trump-air-travel-faa-a638c9651f1fabe8f95d20353779ee5b)

item.title: Expedia Group (travel) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Expedia Group, owner of Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo, confirmed attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider in a supply chain attack that hit several companies. The n0n extortion group claims it stole more than 1 TB of Expedia data. Security researchers had described a similar attack using access tied to the Qubole data platform; Expedia has not named the vendor. Impact: Not disclosed by Expedia. n0n claims (unverified) hundreds of millions of account records and about 830 million rows of loyalty program data, plus traveler profiles and trip records. Status: Breach confirmed by Expedia. Scale and n0n's data claims unconfirmed; investigation ongoing. Sources: Skift (https://skift.com/2026/11/12/expedia-confirms-cyberattack-through-third-party-vendor/); Security Affairs (https://securityaffairs.com/203062/cyber-crime/extortion-group-claims-theft-of-nearly-one-billion-expedia-traveler-records.html)

item.title: RIKEN Fugaku supercomputer (Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: An outsider broke into the internal network that runs Japan's Fugaku supercomputer through a public status dashboard, tampered with internal servers, and took or may have taken user data. RIKEN shut Fugaku down to contain it. Impact: Up to 4,597 Fugaku and RIKYU users' names, email addresses and user IDs, plus credentials users had stored for other systems (such as SSH keys). Fugaku operations suspended and all jobs halted. Status: Confirmed by RIKEN. Investigation ongoing. Sources: RIKEN notice (https://www.riken.jp/en/news_pubs/news/2026/20261116_2/index.html)

item.title: Lyko (beauty retailer, Sweden) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Unauthorized parties got into a small, isolated part of Swedish beauty retailer Lyko's systems and accessed customer data. Lyko says it stopped the breach within an hour and fixed the security hole. Impact: About 60,000 customers across Lyko's markets (36,000 in Sweden): names, addresses and phone numbers. Order information for 95 customers. No ID numbers, payment details or passwords. Status: Confirmed by Lyko. Reported to Sweden's privacy regulator (IMY). Sources: Lyko press release (PDF) (https://storage.mfn.se/d6ebc8eb-0ad4-4a6b-8b5f-12ea0d0050bb/lyko-has-addressed-a-data-breach-in-a-limited-part-of-its-system.pdf); SVT Nyheter (Swedish) (https://www.svt.se/nyheter/inrikes/lyko-hackat-kundernas-personuppgifter-har-stulits)

item.title: Microsoft 365 / Outlook global outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services went down worldwide for most of a business day, one of the largest outages in the company's history. Microsoft publicly pushed back on speculation that it had been hacked. What people speculated: A cyberattack on Microsoft's cloud. Official explanation: Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report calls it "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents": a hidden bug from a July update, extra traffic after a Teams failover, and about 14% of gateway servers already offline combined to freeze its gateway servers. Impact: At the worst point more than 80% of the affected gateway servers stopped responding; it took nearly 24 hours to stabilize email. Status: Official cause published. Not a hack. Sources: Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/gadgets/2026/11/microsoft-details-how-three-problems-combined-for-a-global-outage/); BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/microsoft/microsoft-says-months-old-bug-caused-global-microsoft-365-outage/); USA Today (https://www.usatoday.com/story/tech/2026/11/13/microsoft-dismisses-cyberattack-speculation-amid-outage/92759759007/)

item.title: Rakuten Securities (online brokerage, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers got into a test-environment system at Rakuten Securities on Nov. 11 and customer data held there may have been taken. The company detected the intrusion on Nov. 16 and blocked it. Impact: Login IDs and customer codes for up to about 11.25 million accounts; names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, emails, employers, withdrawal bank accounts, and self-reported income and assets for up to about 4.47 million accounts. Rakuten says passwords and PINs were not leaked and no unauthorized trades have been found. Status: Confirmed by Rakuten Securities. Investigation ongoing. Sources: Rakuten Securities announcement (Japanese) (https://www.rakuten-sec.co.jp/web/company/newsrelease/pdf/press2026111702.pdf); The Japan Times (https://www.japantimes.co.jp/business/2026/11/18/companies/rakuten-securities-unauthorized-access/); NHK World (https://www3.nhk.or.jp/nhkworld/news/20261117de77429/)

item.title: Maersk (shipping) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The shipping giant confirmed that a threat actor breached a legacy system belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claimed the attack and threatened to release about 100GB of data, demanding $5 million (attacker's claim). Impact: Maersk says the incident is isolated to a local system, current evidence indicates no sensitive data was disclosed, and shipping operations are not disrupted. Status: Confirmed by Maersk. Investigation ongoing. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/maersk-confirms-data-breach-as-whitearmor-ransomware-demands-5-million/)

item.title: Meetsmore (service booking platform, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers logged into 201 accounts using passwords stolen elsewhere, then exploited a flaw in a scheduling feature to pull customer job details. Impact: Up to 366,850 records with customer addresses, phone numbers and request details. No names, emails, passwords or card numbers. Status: Confirmed by Meetsmore. Flaw fixed. Sources: Meetsmore notice (Japanese) (https://company.meetsmore.com/page/notice-20261116)

item.title: Ipsos (market research) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The global market research firm found a breach of one internal information system and filed a complaint with authorities. Impact: One internal system. Ipsos says operations weren't affected and the scope is still under investigation. Status: Confirmed by Ipsos. Investigation ongoing. Sources: Ipsos statement (https://www.ipsos.com/en/ipsos-announced-it-filed-complaint-regarding-breach-one-its-internal-systems)

item.title: Monadnock Community Hospital (New Hampshire) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A week-long systems outage at the Peterborough, N.H. hospital was caused by a cyber incident, hospital leadership said. Phones and other systems went down and ambulances were diverted from the ER. Impact: Phones and other systems down since Nov. 9; ambulances diverted; some elective major surgeries canceled until Nov. 23. Whether data was taken is still under investigation. Status: Confirmed by the hospital. Law enforcement involved. Investigation ongoing. Sources: Monadnock Ledger-Transcript (https://ledgertranscript.com/2026/11/17/monadnock-community-hospital-cyber-incident/)

item.title: Openlogi (shipping and fulfillment service, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: An outside party broke into systems at Openlogi, a Japanese warehouse and shipping service used by online stores, on Nov. 8-9 and took shipping data. Store clients including Kashima Antlers FC, United Arrows' overseas shops and REALITY Studios have since warned their customers. Impact: Recipient names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and product details from shipments requested Apr. 8 to Nov. 8, 2026. Total count still under investigation; Kashima Antlers alone reports 40,844 affected people. No credit card numbers. Status: Confirmed by Openlogi and client companies. Access route blocked Nov. 9. Sources: Openlogi notice (Japanese) (https://corp.openlogi.com/news/notice-20261111/); Kashima Antlers notice (https://www.antlers.co.jp/en-world/blogs/news/261118ytxj2u)

item.title: Nitori (furniture retailer, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Japan's biggest furniture chain found intruders in a company system and says customer and order records may have been stolen. Impact: Up to 37.62 million potentially affected records (names, contact details, dates of birth); Nitori says the count includes duplicates and is not the number of people. No passwords or card numbers. Status: Confirmed by Nitori, which says attackers extracted data through a vulnerability in an online-shop admin server. How much leaked is still undetermined. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/japanese-furniture-giant-nitori-says-hackers-stole-376m-customer-records/); SC Media (https://www.scworld.com/brief/nitori-reports-data-breach-affecting-37-62-million-customer-records); MLex (https://www.mlex.com/mlex/data-privacy-security/articles/2551466/japan-s-nitori-confirms-data-extraction-says-breach-scope-unclear)

item.title: Port of Santos authority (Brazil) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A cyberattack hit the Santos Port Authority (APS), the state-owned company that runs Brazil's largest port, knocking its online systems partly offline after a power outage at its headquarters. APS later confirmed a ransom demand. Brazil's Federal Police are investigating. Impact: Port authority systems partly down for days; operators reported delays and manual scheduling, arrival records and billing. Terminals and ship movements kept running. APS says it does not know whether data was accessed. Status: Confirmed by the port authority. Recovery ongoing; attacker not officially named. Sources: Folha de S.Paulo (https://www1.folha.uol.com.br/internacional/en/business/2026/11/port-of-santos-confirms-cyberattack-says-it-does-not-know-whether-data-was-accessed-without-authorization.shtml); G1 (Portuguese) (https://g1.globo.com/sp/santos-regiao/porto-mar/noticia/2026/11/12/porto-de-santos-confirma-pedido-de-resgate-apos-ataque-hacker-7percent-dos-dados-foram-recuperados.ghtml)

item.title: M1 (mobile carrier, Singapore) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Singapore mobile carrier M1 disclosed a data breach it identified on October 30 involving customer information. It says the breach has been contained. Impact: Customer names, NRIC/FIN numbers, dates of birth, mobile numbers, email addresses and addresses. M1 says no payment card, banking or account access was compromised; it has not said how many customers are affected. Status: Confirmed by M1. Customers being notified. Sources: M1 (https://www.m1.com.sg/about-us/news-releases/2026/m1-discloses-data-breach)

item.title: The Kyiv Independent (news outlet) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers got into the newsroom's website system and newsletter service, posting and emailing fake claims about Zelensky and Putin. The outlet suspects Russia. Impact: Four fake emails sent to readers and fake posts on the site (removed). Payment data not at risk. Status: Confirmed by The Kyiv Independent. Sources: The Kyiv Independent (https://kyivindependent.com/kyiv-independent-hit-by-suspected-russian-cyberattack/); Ukrainska Pravda (https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/04/8061264/)

item.title: SPH Media (news publisher, Singapore) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: SPH Media, publisher of The Straits Times, found cyberattacks on five of its systems between Nov. 4 and Nov. 8, which it believes were carried out by the same threat actor. It says software bugs and system configuration played a part. Impact: About 9% of its database exposed, mostly email addresses plus some names, mailing addresses and phone numbers. No payment card, banking or account access data compromised. Status: Confirmed by SPH Media. Reported to Singapore authorities and police. Sources: SPH Media statement (https://www.sph.com.sg/media-centre/media-releases/media-statement-sph-cybersecurity-incident/); The Straits Times (https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/politics/sph-media-hit-by-cyberattacks-no-payment-card-details-or-financial-information-compromised)

item.title: Air Botswana — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Botswana's state-owned airline said unauthorized parties got into some of its internal systems in what it described as a suspected ransomware attack. Impact: Affected systems hold employee and internal information. The airline says passenger bookings, aircraft systems and flight operations were not affected. It has not said whether data was copied. Status: Confirmed by Air Botswana. Investigation ongoing; authorities engaged. Sources: ITWeb Africa (https://itweb.africa/article/air-botswana-probes-suspected-cyberattack/GxwQDq1DLy8MlPVo); CIO Africa (https://cioafrica.co/air-botswana-reports-suspected-ransomware-attack-on-internal-systems/)

item.title: Myriad Genetics (genetic testing) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Myriad Genetics detected unauthorized access to its IT network and temporarily suspended testing operations and order management systems while it contained the activity. Impact: Testing temporarily paused. The company is still assessing whether patient records were accessed. Most systems back to normal. Status: Confirmed by Myriad Genetics (SEC filing). Investigation ongoing. Sources: SEC 8-K filing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/899923/000162828026070659/mygn-20261102.htm); Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/myriad-genetics-reports-unauthorized-access-to-it-network-resumes-most-operations-93CH-5004615)

item.title: Ukraine air raid alert app — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers pushed fake nuclear and chemical attack warnings to users of Ukraine's air raid alert app. President Zelensky called it a Russian cyberattack. Impact: Several fake alerts sent to users' phones before being cleared about an hour later. Status: Confirmed by Ukraine's government. Sources: The Kyiv Independent (https://kyivindependent.com/kyiv-independent-hit-by-suspected-russian-cyberattack/)

item.title: Binance (crypto exchange) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers drained about $6.3 billion in crypto from Binance's hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record. Blockchain analysts traced it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group. Impact: About $6.3 billion stolen. Binance says it covered all losses and resumed withdrawals. Status: Confirmed by Binance. Losses covered. Sources: Binance announcement (https://www.binance.com/en/support/announcement/detail/c5a8729a97ac486d963784d96c5642d7); CNBC (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-coverage-withdrawals.html); Chainalysis (https://www.chainalysis.com/blog/binance-exploit-latest-findings-and-response/)

item.title: Cursor (code editor, via Fireworks AI) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Cursor said attackers used an access key stolen from its provider Fireworks AI to copy stored data, then used credentials found in that data to get into other internal systems. On Oct. 29 they used a stolen credential to put malicious copies of a popular extension on Cursor's extension marketplace for about 11 hours. Impact: Up to about 5,000 developers may have downloaded the malicious extension, which tried to install hidden SSH backdoors. Cursor says fewer than 0.05% of users had stored coding traces exposed and some customer support data, contact details and archived non-production code were taken. Status: Confirmed by Cursor in an incident report (Nov. 14). Exposed credentials rotated and marketplace rebuilt. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cursor-confirms-security-breach-led-to-malicious-claude-code-extension/)

item.title: ARARA (email delivery service, Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers broke into a Japanese newsletter service used by hundreds of brands, including SEGA, and took subscriber email lists. Impact: 81,329,467 email addresses from up to about 380 client companies (company count; addresses, not people). Status: Confirmed by ARARA. Investigation ongoing. Sources: ARARA report (Japanese) (https://www.arara.com/dcms_media/other/arara_20261106.pdf); BleepingComputer (SEGA) (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/sega-newsletter-data-breach-exposes-22-million-email-addresses/)

item.title: University of Texas at Arlington — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers broke into University of Texas at Arlington systems in late October. The school took down MachForms, its online forms portal for event registration, service requests and surveys, and later confirmed that personal information was stolen. The Qilin ransomware gang claimed the attack. Impact: Personal information of students and employees stolen; the school has not said what data or how many people. MachForms still offline as of Nov. 13. Status: Confirmed by the university. Qilin's claim not confirmed by the school. Sources: The Record (https://therecord.media/university-of-texas-arlington-warns-data-breach); The Shorthorn (https://www.theshorthorn.com/news/campus/uta-cybersecurity-investigation-finds-that-personal-information-was-accessed/article_1807ba67-877b-419f-9810-da2c32afa187.html)

item.title: J.B. Hunt (trucking) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: J.B. Hunt confirmed it is investigating unauthorized access to certain information in an isolated part of its technology systems. The WhiteArmor extortion group claims it stole data from J.B. Hunt as well as Ryder and Echo Global Logistics; those two have not publicly confirmed an incident. Impact: Systems stayed operational. What was taken has not been disclosed; employees have filed multiple proposed class action lawsuits. The date shown is when ransomware trackers recorded the attack. Status: Confirmed by J.B. Hunt. Investigation ongoing. Sources: FreightWaves (https://www.freightwaves.com/news/new-cyber-thief-gang-targets-transports-hunt-ryder-and-echo-hit); Breach News (https://breachnews.com/ransomware/jb-hunt-ryder-echo-whitearmor-ransomware-claims/)

item.title: ConnectWise (IT management software) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Chinese state-linked hackers stole credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service and used them to get into customers' Microsoft 365 accounts, spying on thousands of companies. Impact: Customer Microsoft 365 tenants (email and files) potentially accessed; Cloud Backup taken offline. Status: Confirmed by ConnectWise and Microsoft. Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/22/chinese-hackers-spied-on-thousands-of-companies-after-breaching-it-giant-connectwise/); The Hacker News (https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/connectwise-resets-credentials-as-cloud.html)

item.title: Uber drivers (via Fireworks AI) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers breached Fireworks AI, a tech provider, and used stolen credentials to reach Uber data. Notion was also affected. Impact: 149,346 Uber drivers notified (names, addresses, birth dates, license numbers). Status: Confirmed by Uber, Fireworks AI and Notion. Sources: TechCrunch (Uber) (https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/16/uber-confirms-hackers-stole-thousands-of-drivers-license-information-in-data-breach/); TechCrunch (Fireworks/Notion) (https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/cyberattack-on-fireworks-ai-allowed-hackers-to-access-notion-customers-chat-transcripts/)

item.title: Fandango (movie tickets) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Card-skimming code was planted on Fandango's website checkout page and sent payment details typed in by customers to the attackers. Impact: Card numbers, CVV codes, expiration dates, billing ZIP codes and email addresses for purchases made October 8-11, 2026. Fandango has not said how many customers were affected. Status: Confirmed by Fandango. Notices sent. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/fandango-says-hackers-stole-payment-card-details-from-checkout-pages/)

item.title: IDC Frontier cloud (Japan) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Ransomware hit a SoftBank-group cloud provider, encrypting customer virtual servers used by companies and local governments. Impact: 495 companies and local governments disrupted. Status: Confirmed by IDC Frontier. No ransom paid. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/ransomware-attack-disrupts-japans-idcf-cloud-used-by-govt-clients/); IDC Frontier update (https://www.idcf.jp/pdf/topics/20261027/20261027_IDCF_UA_Update7_EN.pdf)

item.title: Irish credit unions (via Wellington IT) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: An attacker exploited a flaw in the online banking platform Wellington IT provides to Irish credit unions and pulled saved payee records in early October. Credit unions were only told in mid-November. Impact: About 40 credit unions affected, roughly a quarter of the country's total. Saved payee names, IBANs, BICs, addresses and payment references potentially exposed. Officials say member balances were not accessed and no financial losses have been reported. Status: Confirmed by affected credit unions and Ireland's government. Flaw closed. Assessment ongoing. Sources: RTÉ (https://www.rte.ie/news/2026/1118/1599645-credit-union-data-breach-assessed/); Irish Department of Finance (https://www.gov.ie/en/department-of-finance/press-releases/t%C3%A1naiste-and-minister-troy-comment-on-suspected-cybersecurity-incident-involving-credit-unions/); Galway Live (https://www.ireland-live.ie/west/galway-live/galway-credit-union-cyberattack-9358558)

item.title: The Japan Times (news outlet) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Ransomware hit an old administrative file server at The Japan Times' group, and data the attacker claimed to have stolen was later posted online. Impact: HR and business-partner records from 2001 to August 2022 may be included; reader and payment systems were separate. Status: Confirmed by The Japan Times. Sources: The Japan Times notice (https://www.japantimes.co.jp/press/2026/10/19/notice-ransomware-incident-second-report/)

item.title: DriveWealth (brokerage tech) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: An intruder got into DriveWealth's network, which powers investing features in many apps, and accessed customer data including Social Security numbers. Impact: 30 million people (state attorney general filings). Status: Confirmed. Notices sent. Sources: California AG notice (https://oag.ca.gov/system/files/DriveWealth%20-%20Redacted%20Notice.pdf); Washington AG (https://www.atg.wa.gov/drivewealth-llc)

item.title: IDScan.net (ID verification) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A company that scans driver's licenses for bars, stores and other businesses confirmed hackers copied ID data from its cloud. Hackers advertised photos of more than 150 million North American drivers. Impact: 13 million people per a state filing; hackers claimed about 153 million records. Status: Confirmed by IDScan.net. Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/10/id-verification-giant-idscan-confirms-data-breach-with-more-than-150-million-drivers-licenses-stolen/); Help Net Security (https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/11/idscan-net-data-breach-153-million-drivers-licenses/)

item.title: ATF (U.S. firearms agency) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The ATF declared a "major incident" after a breach of a standalone system holding information on targets of its investigations. A ransomware gang (Qilin) claimed it; ATF has not confirmed who did it. Impact: One standalone system; data taken not disclosed. Status: Confirmed by ATF. Investigation ongoing. Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/08/27/atf-declares-major-incident-as-ransomware-gang-claims-hack/); The Record (https://therecord.media/doj-atf-cyberattack-qilin-ransomware)

item.title: Boston Scientific (medical devices) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A cyberattack knocked out Boston Scientific's global network, halting manufacturing, orders and shipping for about two weeks. Impact: Global operations disrupted until about September 9; expected material hit to 2026 results. Status: Confirmed by Boston Scientific. Recovered. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/boston-scientific-hit-by-cyberattack-global-operations-affected-2026-08-26/); Boston Scientific update (https://news.bostonscientific.com/update-on-recent-cybersecurity-incident)

item.title: American Airlines nationwide ground stop — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: The FAA briefly stopped all American Airlines departures nationwide after an IT problem. It came during a week of several big outages. What people speculated: A cyberattack, possibly part of a wider campaign that week. Official explanation: American described a technology issue affecting connectivity for some systems. It has not named a cause, and there is no public evidence of an attack. Impact: Nationwide departure halt of roughly 45 minutes, with delays after. Status: No root cause published. No evidence of a hack. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/world/faa-issues-american-airlines-nationwide-ground-stop-over-it-outage-2026-07-28/); RVA Cyber analysis (https://news.rvacyber.com/briefings/major-outages-cyber-assessment-july-2026/)

item.title: Xbox sign-in and game library outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Xbox players couldn't sign in, buy or launch games for many hours; even some disc games failed license checks. What people speculated: An attack on Microsoft's gaming network during a cluster of outages. Official explanation: Microsoft's Xbox CTO said a licensing service that Xbox depends on began failing. Impact: Sign-in, purchase and game launch failures from late July 26 into July 27. Status: Company explanation given. Not attributed to a hack. Sources: RVA Cyber analysis (https://news.rvacyber.com/briefings/major-outages-cyber-assessment-july-2026/)

item.title: PlayStation Network outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: PlayStation Network accounts, gaming, the store and other features were down for about five hours. What people speculated: A hack of Sony's network. Official explanation: Sony has not published a root cause. Some outlets speculated about a cloud provider problem, which Sony did not confirm. Impact: About five hours of disruption across PSN services. Status: Cause not disclosed. No public evidence of a hack. Sources: RVA Cyber analysis (https://news.rvacyber.com/briefings/major-outages-cyber-assessment-july-2026/)

item.title: fairlife / Coca-Cola — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A ransomware attack on production systems forced Coca-Cola to pause fairlife milk production at all four U.S. plants. Impact: U.S. production suspended; most production resumed by July 27. Status: Confirmed by Coca-Cola (SEC filing). Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/16/coca-cola-suspended-production-at-its-fairlife-dairy-after-a-ransomware-attack/); AP News (https://apnews.com/article/fairlife-milk-cyberattack-cocacola-e3a5574043f58a7340500c89d74c2ba6)

item.title: Klue (market research software) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers used an old Klue credential to steal access keys, then pulled sales/CRM data from many Klue customers, including security companies like HackerOne and LastPass. Impact: Close to 200 customer companies affected (TechCrunch); business contact and sales data. Status: Confirmed by Klue and affected companies. Sources: TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/06/22/klue-hack-results-in-data-breach-at-several-cybersecurity-firms/); HackerOne advisory (https://www.hackerone.com/security-updates/klue-2026-06)

item.title: DentaQuest (dental benefits) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers were inside DentaQuest's network for several days and stole personal and health data. It is the largest healthcare breach reported to U.S. regulators this year. Impact: 15 million people (HHS filing). Status: Confirmed. Notices sent. Sources: Healthcare Dive (https://www.healthcaredive.com/news/Dental-benefits-administrator-discloses-breach/827533/); TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/15/the-worst-hacks-and-breaches-of-2026-so-far/)

item.title: Instructure (Canvas learning platform) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The ShinyHunters gang stole data from Canvas, the school platform used by thousands of schools and universities, then defaced login pages during finals. Instructure later reached an agreement with the hackers. Impact: Names, emails, student IDs and some private messages. Hackers claimed 275 million users; TechCrunch reported more than 30 million students and staff. Status: Confirmed by Instructure. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/instructure-confirms-data-breach-shinyhunters-claims-attack/); TechCrunch (https://techcrunch.com/2026/05/07/hackers-deface-school-login-pages-after-claiming-another-instructure-hack/); Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/canvas-parent-company-reaches-agreement-with-hacking-group-behind-recent-breach-2026-05-12/)

item.title: Carnival Corporation (cruises) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers tricked their way into an employee account and copied customer data. ShinyHunters claimed the attack; Carnival hasn't named a group. Impact: 5,995,277 people; data may include government ID numbers. Status: Confirmed by Carnival. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/carnival-cruise-confirms-data-breach-affecting-nearly-6-million-people/); The Record (https://therecord.media/cruise-giant-carnival-confirms-data-breach-affecting-6-million)

item.title: U.S. water systems (Iran-linked) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: U.S. agencies warned that Iran-affiliated hackers were breaking into internet-exposed control equipment (PLCs) at water and wastewater systems and other critical infrastructure, causing operational disruption. Impact: Operational disruption at affected utilities; no single total published. Status: Confirmed by CISA, FBI, EPA and NSA advisories. Sources: CISA advisory AA26-097A (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/cybersecurity-advisories/aa26-097a); EPA (https://www.epa.gov/newsreleases/epa-fbi-cisa-nsa-issue-joint-cybersecurity-advisory-water-system-regarding-iranian)

item.title: FBI surveillance system — Confirmed Hack
item.description: The FBI declared a "major cyber incident" and notified Congress after a suspected China-linked breach of a system tied to wiretaps and surveillance targets. Impact: Possible exposure of surveillance-target information; full scope not disclosed. Status: Confirmed by the FBI. Investigation ongoing. Sources: POLITICO (https://www.politico.com/news/2026/04/01/fbi-hack-surveillance-system-major-incident-00854237); NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/fbi-labels-suspected-china-hack-law-enforcement-data-major-cyber-incid-rcna266495)

item.title: Stryker (medical technology) — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Iran-linked hackers (Handala) took over admin accounts and remotely wiped tens of thousands of company devices, disrupting operations for weeks. Impact: Roughly 80,000 devices wiped (BleepingComputer); fully operational again about three weeks later. Status: Confirmed by Stryker. Recovered. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/medtech-giant-stryker-fully-operational-after-data-wiping-attack/); Krebs on Security (https://krebsonsecurity.com/2026/03/iran-backed-hackers-claim-wiper-attack-on-medtech-firm-stryker/)

item.title: European Commission cloud — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Hackers poisoned an update of Trivy, a popular security tool, to steal a European Commission cloud key, then took data from its cloud accounts. Impact: About 340 GB of data, including personal data and email content; data of 30 EU entities exposed (CERT-EU). Status: Confirmed by CERT-EU and the Commission. Sources: CERT-EU (https://cert.europa.eu/blog/european-commission-cloud-breach-trivy-supply-chain); BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cert-eu-european-commission-hack-exposes-data-of-30-eu-entities/)

item.title: Cisco SD-WAN zero-day attacks — Confirmed Hack
item.description: Attackers exploited unknown flaws in Cisco's SD-WAN network gear to get admin control. CISA ordered federal agencies to patch within two days and hunt for intruders. Impact: Unknown number of networks; Cisco Talos said the campaign went back to at least 2023. Status: Confirmed by Cisco and CISA (Emergency Directive 26-03). Sources: CISA ED 26-03 (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/news/immediate-action-required-cisa-issues-emergency-directive-secure-cisco-sd-wan-systems); Cybersecurity Dive (https://www.cybersecuritydive.com/news/cisa-emergency-directive-cisco-sd-wan-devices/813110/)

item.title: Verizon nationwide wireless outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Verizon customers across the U.S. lost wireless service for hours. What people speculated: A cyberattack on the phone network. Official explanation: Verizon blamed a "software issue"; reports cited law-enforcement sources saying there was no indication of a cyberattack. Verizon offered affected customers a $20 credit. Impact: Hours-long loss of service for customers nationwide. Status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack. Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/mobile/verizon-blames-nationwide-outage-on-a-software-issue/); Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/verizon-offers-20-credit-customers-affected-by-massive-wireless-outage-2026-01-15/)

item.title: Poland's energy sector — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A coordinated, destructive attack hit more than 30 wind and solar farms and a major combined heat and power plant. Poland's CERT linked it to Russian state hackers. Impact: Communications disrupted at some grid connection points; power and heat generation did not stop. Status: Confirmed by CERT Polska and the Polish government. Sources: CERT Polska report (https://cert.pl/en/posts/2026/01/incident-report-energy-sector-2025/); The Hacker News (https://thehackernews.com/2026/01/poland-attributes-december-cyber.html)

item.title: Cloudflare global outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Cloudflare, which sits in front of a huge share of websites, broke much of the web for several hours, including ChatGPT. Even Cloudflare's own team first suspected a massive DDoS attack. What people speculated: A huge DDoS (traffic-flood) attack. Official explanation: Cloudflare's postmortem says a database permission change made a configuration file for its bot-blocking system double in size, which crashed its core proxy software. Impact: Errors on a large share of websites using Cloudflare for several hours. Status: Official cause published. Not a hack. Sources: Cloudflare postmortem (https://blog.cloudflare.com/18-november-2025-outage/); Ars Technica (https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2025/11/cloudflare-broke-much-of-the-internet-with-a-corrupted-bot-management-file/)

item.title: Amazon Web Services (US-EAST-1) — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: A failure in Amazon's biggest cloud region took down a long list of apps and websites for hours, leading many people to wonder if it was an attack on internet infrastructure. What people speculated: A cyberattack or DNS hijacking. Official explanation: AWS traced it to a hidden race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management that left a key DNS record empty. There was no sign of malicious activity. Impact: Widespread disruption to sites and apps that rely on AWS. Status: Official cause published. Not a hack. Sources: BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cev1en9077ro); WIRED (https://www.wired.com/story/what-that-huge-aws-outage-reveals-about-the-internet/)

item.title: Jaguar Land Rover — Confirmed Hack
item.description: A cyberattack forced JLR to shut down car production for about six weeks. It later reported a heavy loss tied to the attack. Impact: £196 million in costs reported for the quarter; production halted for weeks. Status: Confirmed by JLR. Recovered. (Older event, still in the news.) Sources: BleepingComputer (https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/jaguar-land-rover-cyberattack-cost-the-company-over-220-million/); BBC News (https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/ckg1w255gy1o)

item.title: Starlink global outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet went down worldwide for hours, prompting talk of an attack. What people speculated: A cyberattack on the satellite network. Official explanation: SpaceX said a failed software upgrade to its ground-based network systems caused the outage. Impact: Global loss of Starlink service for hours. Status: Company explanation given. Not a hack. Sources: Reuters (https://www.reuters.com/technology/spacex-probes-cause-starlinks-global-satellite-network-outage-2025-07-25/); PCMag (https://me.pcmag.com/en/networking/31409/spacex-traces-starlink-outage-to-network-upgrade)

item.title: Spain & Portugal blackout — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: Nearly all of mainland Spain and Portugal lost power. In the first hours, a cyberattack was one of the theories openly discussed. What people speculated: A cyberattack on the power grid. Official explanation: Spain's government report (June 2025) and the European grid operators' expert panel final report (March 2026) found no evidence of a cyberattack. They blame voltage control problems and a chain of generator disconnections. Impact: Power cut across the Iberian Peninsula. Status: Official reports published. No cyberattack found. (Older event, final report in 2026.) Sources: The Guardian (https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/jun/17/expert-report-rules-out-cyber-attack-for-spain-and-portugal-april-blackout); ENTSO-E final report (https://www.entsoe.eu/news/2026/03/20/entso-e-publishes-expert-panel-final-report-on-28-april-2025-blackout-in-spain-and-portugal/)

item.title: CrowdStrike / Windows global IT outage — Speculated / Potential Hack
item.description: A single update from security company CrowdStrike crashed Windows computers around the world, grounding flights and knocking banks, hospitals and broadcasters offline. It is still the go-to comparison whenever a big outage hits. What people speculated: A global cyberattack. Official explanation: CrowdStrike said the same day it was not a cyberattack. A faulty content update for its Falcon sensor caused Windows machines to crash. Impact: About 8.5 million Windows devices (Microsoft estimate). Status: Official cause published. Not a hack. (Older event, still widely referenced.) Sources: CrowdStrike technical details (https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/falcon-update-for-windows-hosts-technical-details/); Microsoft (https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/07/20/helping-our-customers-through-the-crowdstrike-outage/)
